sentences.text: JUDGMENT
This petition under Section 166 MV Act is filed seeking compensation of .15,00,000/- for the injuries sustained by the Petitioner in a road traffic accident.

2. It is stated that on 19.03.2022 about 1.00 p.m., to 3.30 p.m. the Petitioner was riding the Bajaj Discovery vehicle bearing Reg. No.KA-50- E-4846 along with his wife as a pillion rider on Ravi Kumar.B vs K.S.R.T.C on 8 April, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/94123342/
1 Vijayapura H Cross Road, near Sri. Duggamma temple, J.Venkatapura lake, Shidlaghatta Taluk,
Chikkaballapura District, at that time the driver of KSRTC Bus bearing Reg. No.KA- 40-F-0892 came from the opposite direction in a rash and negligent manner, due to which the middle side body of the said bus knocked to the petitioner vehicle, due to impact, petitioner and pillion rider fell down and sustained grievous injuries.
He was immediately taken to Vijayapura Government hospital, after first aid treatment he was shifted to Baptist Hospital, Bengaluru, wherein he has taken treatment as an 2nd inpatient.
Due to accidental injuries he is suffering from permanent disability and is unable to lead normal life as earlier.
It is claimed that Petitioner has spent amount of Rs.3,00,000/- for treatment, medicines, conveyance and other charges.
At the time of accident, Petitioner was aged 37 years, working as a Weaver and was earning .25,000/- p.m.
Due to accidental injuries he has lost his earning capacity and income.
As the accident was caused due to negligence of the driver of the offending vehicle, it is requested to award compensation from the Respondent.
3. In response to the petition notice, the Respondent has appeared before the court through his counsel and filed the written statement.
4. The Respondent has appeared before the court and filed the objections denying negligence of its driver.

It has contended that the driver N.Lokesh attached to Doddaballapura Depot,
Chikkaballapura Division on 19.03.2019 was on duty in relation to KSRTC Bus No.KA-40-F-0892plying from Kolar to Doddaballpura, as the duties assigned by the Traffic Controller.
The bus proceeded at 15.15 towards G.Venkatapura lake near Jangamakote.

At that time the rider of two wheeler 2nd bearing No.KA-50-E-4846 with two pillion riders without wearing helmet came from opposite direction overtook the Tata Ace in a rash and negligent manner lost controlled hit the bus on the right side Diesel Tank in order to save the rider the driver had to negotiate the bus towards left side and applied the brake.

The driver and the conductor as also the passenger alighted the bus and saw that the rider of the two wheeler had fallen down and bleeding and the petitioner has contributed his negligence for the occurrence of alleged accident.
It has denied the injuries sustained by the Petitioner, treatment taken by him, disability suffered by him and also the expenses claimed by the Petitioner and prays to dismiss the petition.

5. On the basis of the above pleadings, the following Issues were framed :-
1.

Whether the Petitioner proves that he sustained injuries when he was riding the Bajaj Discovery Motorcycle bearing No.KA- 50-E-4846 on 19.03.2022 about 3.30 p.m., on Vijayapura -H Cross Road, near Sri, Duggamma Temple, J.Venkatapura Lke, Shidlaghatta Taluk, Chikkaballapura District, due to rash and negligent driving by the driver of the KSRTC Bus vehicle bearing No.KA-40-F-0892 ?
2nd 2.
What compensation Petitioner is entitled?

3. What order ?
Ravi Kumar.

7.

8.

9. My findings to the above issues are as under:
Issue No.1: In the Affirmative.
Issue No.2: Partly in affirmative.

Issue No.3: As per the final order, for the following:
REASONS 10. ISSUE NO.1:-
In order to prove his claim, Petitioner relied on the police and medical records.
PW-1 is the injured and the direct witness to the incident.

He has deposed that on 19.03.2022 about 2nd 1.00 p.m., to 3.30 p.m. the Petitioner was riding the Bajaj Discovery vehicle bearing Reg.
No.KA-50- E-4846 along with his wife as a pillion rider on Vijayapura H Cross Road, near Sri.
Duggamma temple, J.Venkatapura lake, Shidlaghatta Taluk, Chikkaballapura District, at that time the driver of KSRTC Bus bearing Reg. No.KA-40-F-0892 came from opposite direction in a rash and negligent manner, due to which the middle side body of the said bus knocked to the petitioner vehicle, due to impact petitioner and pillion rider fell down and sustained grievous injuries.
11. He has produced copy of FIR at Ex.P.1, complaint at Ex.P.2, spot mahazar at Ex.P.3, seizure mahazar at Ex.P.4, IMV report at Ex.P.5 & 6, Wound certificate at Ex.P.7 and charge sheet at Ex.P.8.
As per wound certificate he has sustained Floating Knee right type 3 B open fracture of right distal femur and right proximal tibia.
12. The Respondent has contended that the petitioner was responsible for the alleged accident.

During the course of cross-examination of PW1, learned counsel for the Respondent has put forth suggestion that, due to his daughter sitting on the petrol tank in 2nd the motor cycle, the petitioner was unable to observe on coming vehicles.
He denied the same.
He also denied that he attempted to overtake the lorry, without observing the offending bus, resulting in a collision.

It was further suggested that the offending bus was within the white lane; however, PW1 stated that the accident occurred on a curved road, the three-fourths of bus had turned, the remaining one -fourths of the offending bus knocked his vehicle.
This particular fact has not been denied by the learned counsel for the Respondent by posing suggestions or questions.
13. The conductor of the offending bus was examined as RW1 and he has reiterated the contention of the written statement.
During the course of cross- examination, he denied that the accident occurred due to his negligence.
He admitted that he was the driver of the offending vehicle and FIR was registered against him.

3 14.
After through investigation IO has been filed charge sheet against the offending vehicle.
Absolutely there are no contrary materials.
There are no materials to show that the offending vehicle was not caused the accident and it was not the negligence of driver of the offending vehicle.
It is well settled principle that Motor 2nd Vehicles Act is beneficial legislation, the tribunal need not to go for the strict proof of rash and negligence.
Charge sheet prima-facie establishes that the rash and negligence on the part of the driver of the offending vehicle.
All the records corroborate with the evidence of PW.1.
Thereby the accident occurred and petitioner has sustained injuries in a RTA.
Hence, Issue No.1 is answered in the Affirmative.
15. ISSUE NO.2 :- The Petitioner states that due to the accident he has sustained grievous injuries.

Immediately he was taken to Government hospital, Vijayapura, after first aid treatment he was shifted to Baptist Hospital, Bengaluru, wherein he has taken treatment as an inpatient and underwent surgery and discharged with an advice to take complete bed rest and to continue further follow up treatment.
He has stated that at the time of accident, he was working as an Weaver and was earning .25,000/- p.m.
Due to the accidental injuries he is unable to do his work and continue as earlier and suffered loss of income.
He has lost his normal life as earlier and suffering huge loss of income.
He is facing difficulties in his day-today activities.

PW-2 Dr.B.Ramesh, Orthopedic Surgeon at Victoria Hospital, Bengaluru, has deposed that the Petitioner has sustained injuries in a RTA and treated as an inpatient at Baptist hospital and Petitioner has sustained floating knee right type 3 B open fracture of right distal femur and right proximal tibia.
PW-2 has stated that petitioner was treated wound debridement, Internal fixation of right distal femur and proximal tibia.
PW-2 has examined the Petitioner on 24.09.2024 clinically and radiologically while assessing disability.

He found that Petitioner complains of pain in right knee, cannot squat on floor, sit cross legged, difficult in climbing upstairs, walk on slope cannot kneel, stand on affected limb, difficulty to do routine activities.
On examination he has assessed the permanent physical disability of at 56% and whole body at 28%.
17. PW-2 in his cross-examination has stated that he has not treated the Petitioner.
He denied that in order to help the petitioner, he has assessed the disability on the higher side.
He also denied that the petitioner is not suffering any difficulties as stated in his chief affidavit.
He has assessed the physical disability and not the functional disability.
considering the grievous injury, avocation and considering the difficulties and evidence of PW-2 and also by considering the age of the Petitioner, the functional disability is assessed at 10%.
19 . The Petitioner has stated that he was aged about 37 years, in support of his age he has produced his DL at Ex.P.10, which shows his date of birth as 02.08.1985.
Therefore, as on date of accident his age is considered as 37 years.
Therefore, the proper multiplier applicable to the case on hand is 15.

sentences.text:
The Petitioner has claimed that he was working as an Weaver and was earning .25,000/- p.m.
Due to the accidental injuries, he is unable to do his work and is unable to do his work as earlier and suffering huge loss of income.
However, the petitioner has not produced any documents to substantiate his income.
In the absence of material with regard to source of income, the tribunal has to be considered the notional income chart of the Lok Adalath.
The alleged accident has taken place in the year 2022, the notional income of the injured could be assessed at Rs 15,500/- Per Month.

Thus this tribunal is of the opinion that the petitioner who sustained the injuries is entitled for compensation under the following heads:
22. Loss of future income on account of permanent disability: Looking into the nature of injury, it definitely affects the working capacity of any person.
the Petitioner is auto driver, considering nature of injury and doctor's evidence the total functional disability of the Petitioner is considered at 9%.
Thus, loss of future income comes to Rs.15,500 x 12 x 15 x 10 /100= Rs.2,79,000/- towards loss of future income.
23. Pain and sufferings:

So far as the compensation under non-pecuniary damages are concerned,
considering the fact that the Petitioner has suffered grievous injuries and treated as an inpatient which caused him immeasurable mental agony and pain, I am of the opinion that an amount of .30,000/- would be just and fair compensation under the head of pain and sufferings.
24. Loss of amenities of life:
For loss of amenities of life undoubtedly Petitioner is sure to suffer in his day today activities and face hardships.

Hence, 2nd Petitioner is awarded .25,000/- for Loss of amenities of life, frustration, disappointment, unhappiness and inconvenience etc.
25.
Medical expenses:
Under the pecuniary damages, expenses relating to treatment, hospitalization and medicines, the Petitioner has relied on medical bills for .2,47,260/- at Ex.P.13.
Though counsel for Respondent has cross-examined the PW-1, nothing has been elicited to disprove the medical bills.
On perusal of these medical bills, it reveals that the Petitioner has spent . 2,47,260/- towards medical expenses.
The medical bills appears to be genuine.
Hence, Petitioner is awarded .2,47,260/- towards Medical Expenses.
26. Future medical expenses: PW-2 has stated that the petitioner needs one more surgery for removal of implants and arthritis of knee.
But he has not produced any estimation report.
In the absence of material evidence, it is just and reasonable to award Rs.15,000/- towards future medical expenses.
27. Conveyance, food, nourishment and attendant charges:
Ex.P.9-Discharge summary shows that Petitioner was treated as an inpatient at Bangalore 2nd Baptist hospital, Bengaluru from 19.03.2022 to 26.03.2022 i.e., for 8 days.
Therefore, considering the available medical records, it is just and reasonable to award compensation of .10,000/- under the head of conveyance, food, nourishment and attendant charges.

 laid up period

30. Liability:
Respondent being the owner of the offending bus is liable to pay the above compensation with interest @ 6% p.a. to the Petitioner.
With these observation I answer Issue No.2 partly in the affirmative.
31. ISSUE NO.3 :

In view of the above discussion, reasons stated and findings given to Issue Nos. 1 &
2, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER Claim Petition filed under Sec.166 of M.V.Act is allowed in part with cost.
Petitioner is awarded compensation of .6,52,760/- together with interest @ 6% p.a.
(except future medical expenses) from the date of petition till the date of deposit with the Tribunal.
Respondent shall pay the aforesaid amount within two months from the date of this order.
